overall: The committee violated the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session under Purpose 3 without a litigating position to protect; the Purpose 1 allegation was not supported. Minutes must be released.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee denied an individual's Purpose 1 executive session rights when his reputation, character, and mental health were discussed in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: After review of the executive session minutes, we find that the executive session discussion concerned the Civil Service Appeal and federal lawsuit and was not focused on Mr. Alston’s reputation, character, and mental health.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee had no litigating position to protect and so could not meet in executive session under Purpose 3 on a civil service appeal and federal lawsuit.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated above, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by improperly entering into executive session under Purpose 3 to discuss litigation strategy when it had no litigating position to protect.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
Release the minutes of the March 7, 2019 executive session to the public, without redaction or withholding.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
